sn42.8:1.5: This phrase appears to echo Sūtrakṛtāṅga 1.5.1.4–5. Mahāvīra is quoted as saying that a person who “relentlessly kills movable and immovable beings for the sake of his own comfort, who injures them, who takes what is not freely given, who does not train in self-control, the impudent sinner who, unsated, injures many beings will go to hell” (translation adapted from Jacobi). The use of “relentlessly” (_tivva_, Pali _tibba_, Sanskrit _tīrva_) implies a violent and excessive action.
